---
title: "Example: before and after in Porto Alegre"
description: >
  What-if questions answered without rebuilding the network: a new cycle
  path, congestion and a closed avenue, one more health facility, and a
  change in the fare rules, each with its map and its timing.
---



```{r, include = FALSE}
source("setup.R")
```

A transport plan is a list of changes: a cycle path here, a lane taken from
cars there, a new clinic, a fare rule. Each one asks the same question
twice, before and after. In peabiru the street network is built once, and
the changes that r5r calls *scenarios* are arguments of each routing call:
`new_lts` changes the level of traffic stress cyclists meet on chosen
streets, `new_carspeeds` and `carspeed_scale` change car speeds by street
or by area, and a fare structure is a list of tables that can be edited
before the call. A new school or clinic is not even a change to the
network: it is one more row among the destinations.

This example asks four such questions of Porto Alegre, on the sample data
that comes with r5r, and times each one: a what-if is one routing call
on the network as built, with nothing to edit and rebuild. It was computed on 2026-11-12 with
peabiru 0.0.1; the output shown is what the code
printed. The same steps in Python are in the [Python
example](../../python/example-scenarios/).

## The data

| Data | Source | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| Streets | OpenStreetMap extract of Porto Alegre in r5r 2.5.0's sample data (`poa_osm.pbf`) | ODbL 1.0, © OpenStreetMap contributors |
| Public transport | The EPTC bus and Trensurb train GTFS feeds of r5r's sample (`poa_eptc.zip`, `poa_trensurb.zip`), cut for the sample: the buses run from 11:20 to 17:50 only, so the analyses below leave at 14:00 on Monday 13 May 2019 | distributed in the r5r package, whose licence line is `GPL (>= 3) \| MIT + file LICENSE` |
| Grid | `poa_hexgrid.csv`: 1,227 H3 cells (resolution 9) with population, jobs, schools and health facilities; r5r does not document its sources | distributed in the r5r package, whose licence line is `GPL (>= 3) \| MIT + file LICENSE` |
| Fares | `fares/fares_poa.zip`, r5r's fare structure of the sample | distributed in the r5r package, whose licence line is `GPL (>= 3) \| MIT + file LICENSE` |

All files come from r5r's repository at the tag of version 2.5.0
(`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ipea/r5r/v2.5.0/r-package/inst/extdata/poa/`).
The sample also has an elevation raster, left out here: a call with a
scenario routes without slope costs (as r5r does, with a warning), so
the before and the after would not be comparable.


``` r
library(peabiru)
library(sf)

data_dir <- file.path(Sys.getenv("PEABIRU_EXAMPLE_DATA", "example-data"), "poa")
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ipea/r5r/v2.5.0/r-package/inst/extdata/poa/"
dir.create(file.path(data_dir, "network"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(data_dir, "fares"), showWarnings = FALSE)
for (f in c("poa_osm.pbf", "poa_eptc.zip", "poa_trensurb.zip", "poa_hexgrid.csv",
            "fares/fares_poa.zip")) {
  dest <- file.path(data_dir, f)
  if (!file.exists(dest)) download.file(paste0(url, f), dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
}
for (f in c("poa_osm.pbf", "poa_eptc.zip", "poa_trensurb.zip")) {
  if (!file.exists(file.path(data_dir, "network", f))) file.copy(file.path(data_dir, f), file.path(data_dir, "network"))
}

threads <- 4   # of this laptop's ten cores
build_time <- system.time(network <- build_network(file.path(data_dir, "network"),
                                                   n_threads = threads))[["elapsed"]]
network
#> <peabiru_network>
#>   data path: example-data/poa/network
#>   streets:   26,880 vertices, 66,652 edges
#>   transit:   2 feed(s) (poa_trensurb, poa_eptc), 4,010 stops, 226 patterns, 118 services
#>   elevation: NONE
build_time
#> [1] 1.325

grid <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "poa_hexgrid.csv"))
grid$jobs[is.na(grid$jobs)] <- 0               # 5 cells have no count
grid$healthcare[is.na(grid$healthcare)] <- 0
colSums(grid[, c("population", "jobs", "schools", "healthcare")])
#> population       jobs    schools healthcare 
#>     812935     337921        194        141

# the average over the residents of the grid
per_resident <- function(value, id) weighted.mean(value, grid$population[match(id, grid$id)])
osm <- st_read(file.path(data_dir, "poa_osm.pbf"), "lines", quiet = TRUE)
ways_named <- function(name) osm[!is.na(osm$name) & osm$name == name & !is.na(osm$highway), ]
```

Building the network takes about 1.3 seconds; every
call below is timed the same way, by `system.time()`, on a laptop with ten
cores, four of them used (`n_threads`), and other work running, so the
timings are indications.

## A new cycle path

A cyclist who rides only on streets of low traffic stress (levels 1 and 2
of four, `max_lts = 2`, the default) walks the bicycle on the others. In
this extract Avenida Protásio Alves, the radial avenue east of the centre,
is level 4 from end to end. What if it had a protected cycle path? The
scenario gives its OpenStreetMap ways level 1:


``` r
ways <- ways_named("Avenida Protásio Alves")
path <- data.frame(osm_id = as.numeric(ways$osm_id), lts = 1L)
nrow(path)
#> [1] 94

jobs_by_bike <- function(...) {
  accessibility(network, grid, grid, opportunities_colnames = "jobs",
                mode = "BICYCLE", max_lts = 2, cutoffs = 20, n_threads = threads, ...)
}
t_before <- system.time(before <- jobs_by_bike())[["elapsed"]]
t_after <- system.time(after <- jobs_by_bike(new_lts = path))[["elapsed"]]
gain <- merge(before[, c("id", "accessibility")], after[, c("id", "accessibility")],
              by = "id", suffixes = c("_before", "_after"))
gainers <- gain$id[gain$accessibility_after > gain$accessibility_before]
c(before = per_resident(gain$accessibility_before, gain$id),
  after = per_resident(gain$accessibility_after, gain$id),
  share_gaining = sum(grid$population[grid$id %in% gainers]) / sum(grid$population))
#>        before         after share_gaining 
#>  3.006942e+04  3.107525e+04  3.117592e-01
c(call = t_before, with_scenario = t_after)
#>          call with_scenario 
#>         0.369         0.125
```

The average resident reaches 30,069
jobs within 20 minutes on a low-stress bicycle ride today, and
31,075
with the path; 31%
of residents gain something, all of them along the avenue and the
neighbourhoods on both sides. The gain on average is small because most
of the city's jobs are in the centre, which a low-stress ride from the
east does not reach in 20 minutes either way.

One ride across it, from the east end of the avenue to the Santa Casa
hospital in the centre, before and after:


``` r
ends <- data.frame(id = c("Jardim Carvalho", "Santa Casa"),
                   lon = c(-51.1405, -51.2224), lat = c(-30.0415, -30.03043))
monday <- as.POSIXct("2019-05-13 14:00:00", tz = "America/Sao_Paulo")
ride <- function(...) {
  detailed_itineraries(network, ends[1, ], ends[2, ], mode = "BICYCLE", max_lts = 2,
                       departure_datetime = monday, ...)
}
rides <- rbind(cbind(when = "today", ride()), cbind(when = "with the path", ride(new_lts = path)))
as.data.frame(st_drop_geometry(rides)[, c("when", "total_duration", "total_distance")])
#>            when total_duration total_distance
#> 1         today           86.4          11397
#> 2 with the path           66.6           9476
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.alt = "A map of the east of Porto Alegre with the hexagons that gain access to jobs within 20 minutes by bicycle on low-stress streets if Avenida Protasio Alves had a protected cycle path, and one ride from the east end of the avenue to the centre, today and with the path."}
fig("scenario-cycle-path.svg")
```

The ride today is long for its 11 km because the bicycle is walked
wherever no low-stress street goes the right way; with the path, it
follows the avenue. `new_lts` also takes lines (an `sf` of `LINESTRING`s,
each street taking the level of the nearest line), which is how a planned
route that is not yet in OpenStreetMap is drawn in.

## Congestion and a closed avenue

peabiru's car speeds are free flow: the speed limit of each street, or a
default by its class, with no traffic. Two scenarios change that. The
first slows every street within 2 km of the Mercado Público, in the
centre, to half its speed (a polygon with `scale = 0.5`); the second
closes Avenida Ipiranga, the east–west arterial along the Dilúvio creek,
to cars (speed 0 on its ways).


``` r
centre <- st_transform(st_sfc(st_point(c(-51.22781, -30.02756)), crs = 4326), 31982)
slow_centre <- st_sf(poly_id = "centre", scale = 0.5, priority = 1L,
                     geometry = st_transform(st_buffer(centre, 2000, nQuadSegs = 16), 4326))
ipiranga <- ways_named("Avenida Ipiranga")
closed <- data.frame(osm_id = as.numeric(ipiranga$osm_id), max_speed = 0, speed_type = "km/h")

drive <- function(...) {
  m <- travel_time_matrix(network, grid, grid, mode = "CAR", n_threads = threads, ...)
  m[, c("from_id", "to_id", "travel_time_p50")]
}
t_base <- system.time(base <- drive())[["elapsed"]]
t_slow <- system.time(slow <- drive(new_carspeeds = slow_centre))[["elapsed"]]
t_shut <- system.time(shut <- drive(new_carspeeds = closed))[["elapsed"]]
c(call = t_base, half_speed = t_slow, closed = t_shut)
#>       call half_speed     closed 
#>      0.647      1.797      1.803

change <- function(scenario) {
  m <- merge(base, scenario, by = c("from_id", "to_id"), all.x = TRUE)
  m$travel_time_p50.y[is.na(m$travel_time_p50.y)] <- 120   # no longer within the limit
  d <- m$travel_time_p50.y - m$travel_time_p50.x
  c(mean_minutes = mean(d), pairs_slower = mean(d > 0), longest = max(d))
}
rbind(half_speed = change(slow), closed = change(shut))
#>            mean_minutes pairs_slower longest
#> half_speed    0.3484876    0.1429747       9
#> closed        0.7300184    0.1374294     119
```

Over all 1,483,605 pairs of cells, the slower
centre adds 0.35 minutes on average
and the closed avenue 0.73: small
numbers, because most pairs do not cross either. The maps show where they
fall.

```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.alt = "Two maps of Porto Alegre covered by hexagons coloured by how much longer it takes to drive from each cell to all the others: with half speed in the centre, the centre loses most; with Avenida Ipiranga closed, the cells along the avenue lose most."}
fig("scenario-car.svg")
```

Access to health facilities by car, within 10 minutes:


``` r
health_by_car <- function(...) {
  a <- accessibility(network, grid, grid, opportunities_colnames = "healthcare",
                     mode = "CAR", cutoffs = 10, n_threads = threads, ...)
  per_resident(a$accessibility, a$id)
}
c(today = health_by_car(), half_speed = health_by_car(new_carspeeds = slow_centre),
  closed = health_by_car(new_carspeeds = closed))
#>      today half_speed     closed 
#>   35.51350   32.34681   33.42986
```

And access to public transport by car: in R5, and so in peabiru, a car
trip with `mode = c("CAR", "TRANSIT")` may drive to any stop and board
there, or drive all the way. In this sample the direct drive is always
faster, before and after (one departure per pair, a cell in 25):


``` r
some <- grid[seq(1, nrow(grid), by = 25), ]
legs <- function(...) {
  e <- expanded_travel_time_matrix(network, some, some, mode = c("CAR", "TRANSIT"),
                                   departure_datetime = monday, time_window = 1,
                                   n_threads = threads, ...)
  table(uses_transit = e$routes != "[CAR]")
}
legs()
#> uses_transit
#> FALSE 
#>  2500
legs(new_carspeeds = slow_centre)
#> uses_transit
#> FALSE 
#>  2500
```

So the car-access legs do not change here; on a network where they are
used, a scenario changes them too (it changes every street search from the
origin), but not the egress from the last stop, as in r5r (see the
[scenarios guide](scenarios.html)).

## One more health facility

Where would one more health facility bring the most people within 15
minutes' walk? Not a network scenario at all: the destinations are a data
frame, and one walking matrix from every cell to every cell answers the
question for every candidate site at once.


``` r
t_walk <- system.time(walk <- travel_time_matrix(network, grid, grid, mode = "WALK",
                                                  max_trip_duration = 60,
                                                  n_threads = threads))[["elapsed"]]
nearest <- function(sites) {
  w <- walk[walk$to_id %in% sites, ]
  unname(tapply(w$travel_time_p50, w$from_id, min)[grid$id])   # NA: none within the hour
}
has <- grid$id[grid$healthcare > 0]
today <- nearest(has)
covered <- !is.na(today) & today <= 15

# for each candidate cell, the residents it would bring within 15 minutes
w <- walk[walk$travel_time_p50 <= 15 & !covered[match(walk$from_id, grid$id)], ]
w$people <- grid$population[match(w$from_id, grid$id)]
best <- sort(tapply(w$people, w$to_id, sum), decreasing = TRUE)
head(best, 3)
#> 89a90129ca7ffff 89a90129d73ffff 89a90129dcbffff 
#>           17525           17279           17172

with_one_more <- nearest(c(has, names(best)[1]))
share_15 <- function(t) sum(grid$population[!is.na(t) & t <= 15]) / sum(grid$population)
c(today = share_15(today), with_one_more = share_15(with_one_more))
#>         today with_one_more 
#>     0.7901198     0.8116774
t_walk
#> [1] 0.237
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.alt = "Two maps of Porto Alegre: on the left, hexagons coloured by the walking time to the nearest health facility; on the right, the minutes saved around the cell where one more facility brings the most residents within 15 minutes."}
fig("scenario-health.svg")
```

The best cell brings 17,525 more people
within 15 minutes, and the share of the population within 15 minutes of a
health facility goes from 79.0% to
81.2%. The search is over the cells
of the grid, which are hexagons about 350 m across: it says where to look
for a site, not which plot to buy. The same code with `grid$schools`
finds that schools are already within 15 minutes of
94.7% of
the population, so one more school changes far less.

## A change in the fare rules

The sample fare structure charges R\$ 4.80 for a bus and R\$ 4.50 for the
train; a second bus within an hour brings the pair to R\$ 7.20 (and bus and
train to R\$ 8.37), and only one transfer per trip is discounted. Two
edits of it: every transfer within the hour free (two rides cost the
dearer fare, up to two discounted transfers), and no transfer discount at
all.


``` r
fares <- read_fare_structure(file.path(data_dir, "fares", "fares_poa.zip"))
fares$fares_per_type[, c("type", "fare", "unlimited_transfers")]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   type   fare unlimited_transfers
#>   <chr> <dbl> <lgl>              
#> 1 BUS     4.8 FALSE              
#> 2 RAIL    4.5 TRUE
fares$fares_per_transfer
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   first_leg second_leg  fare
#>   <chr>     <chr>      <dbl>
#> 1 BUS       BUS         7.2 
#> 2 RAIL      BUS         8.37
#> 3 BUS       RAIL        8.37

free <- fares
fare_of <- function(type) fares$fares_per_type$fare[match(type, fares$fares_per_type$type)]
free$fares_per_transfer$fare <- pmax(fare_of(free$fares_per_transfer$first_leg),
                                     fare_of(free$fares_per_transfer$second_leg))
free$max_discounted_transfers <- 2L
none <- fares
none$max_discounted_transfers <- 0L
```

The jobs within 45 minutes by public transport, on average over the
residents, with one fare to spend (`max_fare = 4.8`) and with R\$ 7.20,
under each structure. With a fare structure, public transport is routed by
R5's multi-criteria router, which is far slower than the one-criterion
router used without fares (compare the first timing with the others). The
two are different algorithms and their travel times differ a little, in
both directions, so the reference for the budgets is the second row: the
multi-criteria router with a budget that never binds.


``` r
jobs_by_transit <- function(...) {
  a <- accessibility(network, grid, grid, opportunities_colnames = "jobs",
                     mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"), departure_datetime = monday,
                     time_window = 5, cutoffs = 45, seed = 42, n_threads = threads, ...)
  per_resident(a$accessibility, a$id)
}
timed <- function(...) {
  t <- system.time(v <- jobs_by_transit(...))[["elapsed"]]
  c(jobs = round(v), seconds = round(t, 1))
}
rbind(
  no_fare_structure = timed(),
  any_budget = timed(fare_structure = fares, max_fare = 1000),
  sample_4.80 = timed(fare_structure = fares, max_fare = 4.8),
  free_4.80 = timed(fare_structure = free, max_fare = 4.8),
  none_4.80 = timed(fare_structure = none, max_fare = 4.8),
  sample_7.20 = timed(fare_structure = fares, max_fare = 7.2),
  free_7.20 = timed(fare_structure = free, max_fare = 7.2),
  none_7.20 = timed(fare_structure = none, max_fare = 7.2)
)
#>                     jobs seconds
#> no_fare_structure 196273     0.7
#> any_budget        196456    57.4
#> sample_4.80       159996    46.6
#> free_4.80         196375   269.5
#> none_4.80         159996    28.6
#> sample_7.20       192062    62.0
#> free_7.20         196375   218.7
#> none_7.20         159996    42.5
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.alt = "Bars of the average number of jobs reachable within 45 minutes by public transport under the sample fare structure, free transfers and no transfer discount, for budgets of R$ 4.80 and R$ 7.20, against the access with any budget."}
fig("scenario-fares.svg")
```

With one fare to spend, a trip with a transfer is out of reach under the
sample rules (R\$ 7.20) and in reach when transfers are free, which is
where the difference is. With R\$ 7.20, the sample's discount covers one
transfer, and only the structure without discounts falls behind. (The
structure with free transfers is also the slowest to route, several times
slower than the other two in this run.)

For one trip, `trip_options()` lists the options worth considering, here
by travel time and fare; the best option within one fare changes with
the rules:


``` r
pair <- grid[match(c("89a90129d93ffff", "89a9012b12fffff"), grid$id), ]
options_under <- function(structure) {
  o <- trip_options(network, pair[1, ], pair[2, ], departure_datetime = monday,
                    criteria = c("TIME", "FARE"), fare_structure = structure,
                    itineraries = FALSE)$options
  as.data.frame(o[, c("option", "total_time", "fare", "transfers", "departure_time", "description")])
}
options_under(fares)
#>    option total_time fare transfers departure_time
#> 1       1       48.6 12.0         2       14:00:00
#> 2       2       52.5  7.2         1       14:09:00
#> 3       3       53.5  7.2         1       14:08:00
#> 4       4       54.5  7.2         1       14:07:00
#> 5       5       58.5  7.2         1       14:03:00
#> 6       6       59.5  7.2         1       14:02:00
#> 7       7       61.5  7.2         1       14:00:00
#> 8       8       82.2  4.8         0       14:09:00
#> 9       9       87.2  4.8         0       14:04:00
#> 10     10       91.2  4.8         0       14:00:00
#>                                 description
#> 1  WALK > BUS 493 > BUS T7 > BUS 289 > WALK
#> 2           WALK > BUS 441 > BUS 260 > WALK
#> 3            WALK > BUS T7 > BUS 260 > WALK
#> 4            WALK > BUS T7 > BUS 260 > WALK
#> 5           WALK > BUS 495 > BUS 260 > WALK
#> 6           WALK > BUS 494 > BUS 260 > WALK
#> 7           WALK > BUS 491 > BUS 260 > WALK
#> 8                    WALK > BUS 2802 > WALK
#> 9                    WALK > BUS 2802 > WALK
#> 10                   WALK > BUS 2802 > WALK
options_under(free)
#>   option total_time fare transfers departure_time
#> 1      1       48.6  4.8         2       14:00:00
#> 2      2       52.5  4.8         1       14:09:00
#> 3      3       57.5  4.8         1       14:04:00
#>                                description
#> 1 WALK > BUS 493 > BUS T7 > BUS 289 > WALK
#> 2         WALK > BUS 2802 > BUS 260 > WALK
#> 3         WALK > BUS 2802 > BUS 260 > WALK
```

Under the sample rules, the 49-minute trip with three buses costs R\$ 12.00
and the fastest at one fare is a single bus at 82 minutes; with free
transfers, the 49-minute trip costs one fare.

## What each what-if cost

Every scenario above was one routing call on the network built once, at
the start, in 1.3 seconds; none of them rebuilt it.
For the record, the timings of this run (seconds):


``` r
round(c(build_network = build_time,
        bicycle_access = t_before, bicycle_access_new_lts = t_after,
        car_matrix = t_base, car_matrix_half_speed = t_slow, car_matrix_closed = t_shut,
        walk_matrix_every_facility_site = t_walk), 2)
#>                   build_network                  bicycle_access 
#>                            1.33                            0.37 
#>          bicycle_access_new_lts                      car_matrix 
#>                            0.12                            0.65 
#>           car_matrix_half_speed               car_matrix_closed 
#>                            1.80                            1.80 
#> walk_matrix_every_facility_site 
#>                            0.24
```

A call with a street scenario searches the network directly, without the
contraction hierarchies peabiru keeps for repeated street matrices, so it
can take longer than the same call without one (the car matrix here).
This sample is small and builds in about a second, so what a scenario
saves here is the work of editing the OpenStreetMap file, not time; the
network of the [Helsinki example](helsinki.html) takes about 15
seconds to build, and a what-if on it is still one call.

## Variations

- **Real speeds.** Instead of a polygon, a table of `osm_id`, `max_speed`
  and `speed_type = "km/h"` from measured speeds (GPS traces, a traffic
  model) gives peak-hour car times; `carspeed_scale` scales every street
  the table leaves out.
- **Planned routes.** `new_lts` as lines (`line_id`, `lts`, `priority`)
  takes a cycle network drawn in a GIS, before it exists in
  OpenStreetMap; r5r's sample has one, `poa_ls_lts.rds` (see the
  [scenarios guide](scenarios.html)).
- **Many sites.** The facility search above works for any number of new
  sites at once: add the best cell, recompute `covered`, and repeat.
